title: Adaptive per-layer clipping and sequence-length-aware INT8 weight-only CI regression harness (GPTQ/AWQ)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build an integration + regression CI harness that verifies INT8 weight-only quantization profiles (GPTQ and AWQ variants) using adaptive per-layer clipping and sequence-length aware calibration to reduce tail-case accuracy regressions. This ticket scopes the end-to-end pipeline: profile generation, calibration artifacts, CI smoke canaries, long-run nightly regressions, and automated gating for PRs and canary rollouts. The harness must exercise hardware variability (A100 vs H100), kernel selector differences, and batch/seqlen distributions representative of production traffic.
acceptance_criteria: CI integration that runs profile generation and calibration end-to-end and exits non-zero on accuracy regressions beyond thresholds
Per-layer adaptive clipping implemented as a configurable step in the calibration pipeline and persisted in the profile registry
Sequence-length-aware evaluation suites (short/medium/long) added to nightly and pre-merge matrices
Regression thresholds: <=0.5% relative drop for perplexity on language modeling suite, <=1.0% absolute drop for downstream task F1 on representative evals
Golden-seed deterministic runs for the canonical 7B/13B/70B model set on both GPTQ and AWQ implementations
Dashboard that surfaces delta vs FP16 baseline and previous release with per-layer, per-seqlen breakdown
PR gating in CI: block merges when profile changes fail acceptance checks unless explicit override by ML lead with documented rationale
tasks: Design adaptive clipping algorithm and configuration knobs (clip percentile per-layer, warm-start from FP16 activations)
Integrate seqlen-aware sampler into profile generation to emit per-length calibration statistics
Add GPTQ and AWQ runners to the CI pipeline with deterministic seeds and hardware matrix
Create nightly regression job and long-run stability harness with drift detection
Instrument telemetry to capture per-layer quantization error metrics and downstream eval deltas
Implement automatic rollback / fallback policy hooks for canary failures
Ship a dashboard panel and alerts for regression breaches
notes: Motivation: We've observed sporadic accuracy regressions in long sequences on weight-only INT8 profiles that pass short-seq smoke tests. Hypothesis: layerwise activation distribution tails and sequence-length-induced cache behavior are exposing quantization brittleness.
Design decision: prefer adaptive percentile clipping over global static clipping to preserve head token fidelity in early layers while suppressing outliers in later layers.
Trade-offs: more complex calibration increases profile generation time; to mitigate, we will cache intermediate activation histograms and allow incremental updates.
Hardware matrix: run critical CI steps on both A100(40GB) and H100(80GB) images to catch kernel selection and perf-quant coupling issues.

We will reuse existing profile registry schema but add a new 'calib_metadata.v2' key to store per-layer clipping parameters and seqlen buckets. Backcompat story: older runtimes should ignore unknown keys.
Plan to coordinate with runtime and ops teams for canary rollout policy integration (ENG-42107 referenced for canary plumbing).

2025-11-20 Marcus Nguyen: Added seqlen-aware sampler (short/medium/long buckets) into profile generation. Pushed CI changes to run sampled evals as part of pre-merge smoke for quant-profile changes. Observed one flaky case tied to softmax kernel switching under 512->1024 token transitions; added a targeted test.
Next: stabilize AWQ runner on H100, finalize dashboard panels, and implement PR gating with explicit override flow.

SRE (Monica Ruiz): Add throttling to nightly jobs to avoid contention on shared GPU pools; recommend dedicated small pool for long-run regressions.
Runtime (Jared Kim): Kernel selector should expose deterministic choice when running golden-seed CI; otherwise results will be non-reproducible across hosts.
